title: Rav Chana
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Shabbat 97a: “Rav Chana said that Rav Yehudah said that Shmuel said” — Rav Chana sat and it was difficult for him — Rav Yosef said to him, “The Master teaches it on this…,” etc. But Tosafot’s reading there, 4b, s.v. Zarak, is “Rav Chisda sat.” In Bava Batra 157a: “Rav Chana said: Come and hear — Rav Nachman said to him,” etc. In Chullin 56b: a certain hen at Rav Chana’s house — he sent it before Rav Mattenah, who declared it kosher. He said to him, “But Levi taught…” — he said to him, “There,” etc. Hyman suggests that perhaps he is Rav Chana, son-in-law of Rav Ada bar Ahavah, mentioned in Yevamot 110b, where Rav Nachman said: “I found Rav Ada bar Ahavah and Rav Chana his son-in-law sitting and posing challenges to one another in the market of Pumbedita.”

notes.text: Saved Davidson Shabbat97b gives Rav Yosef’s statement, not a question. Saved Yevamot110b has posing challenges, not making pools. The possible Chana identification remains Hyman’s conjecture; רבי וסף is read Rav Yosef contextually.

The consulted Shabbat 97a–97b preserves Chana’s chain and Yosef’s declarative reply; the folio boundary separates them. Yevamot 110b directly names Chana, Ada bar Ahavah’s son-in-law, in a marketplace discussion. Hyman’s possible identification and the exact Tosafot Chisda reading remain separately attributed.
